children.text: kalyāṇaṃ kamalāpatirdiśatu me yaḥ kaustubhe rādhayā vīkṣya svaṃ pratibimbitaṃ pratiyuvatyeṣeti tarkākulam
children.translated_text: May <s>Kamalāpati</s> grant me blessedness—he whom <s>Rādhā</s>, on seeing her own image reflected in the <s>Kaustubha</s> and becoming confused by the thought, “This is a rival young woman,”

children.text: āśleṣonmukhayāpi mānaparayā manvānayā kaitavaṃ tiryagvakritakaṃdharaṃ valitayā sāsūyam ālokitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: looked at jealously from the corner of her eye, her neck artlessly bent aside, for although she was moving to embrace him, her pride made her suppose it was a deception.

children.text: so 'vyānmām aravindanābha udayad yannābhipadmālayā padmā padmavimīlamīlanavidhiprācīṇyavannetrayoḥ
children.translated_text: May <s>Aravindanābha</s>, the Lotus-naveled Lord, protect me. <s>Padmā</s>, dwelling in the lotus rising from his navel and possessing eyes long practiced in the opening and closing of lotuses,
experienced the pleasures of a play born from simultaneously feeling the two conditions of enjoyment in union and its opposite, because the lotus had become half-closed through contact with her eyes.

children.text: diśyānme 'rdhaśivātanuḥ sa bhagavānnityoditāṃ sampadaṃ śambhur viśvajayaśriyaḥ paravaśīkāraikasatkārmaṇam
children.translated_text: May the blessed <s>Śambhu</s>, whose body is half the goddess <s>Śivā</s>, bestow ever-risen prosperity upon me—the one true rite of subjugation that brings the glory of universal conquest under one's control.

children.text: yatraikāṅganavīnavibhramarasād ekāṅgagupter anāsvādāt sambhavadadbhutaikaparamā jāgarti hemādrijā ||
children.translated_text: In him <s>Hemādrijā</s>, the Daughter of the Snow Mountain, shines as a singular supreme marvel, arising from the delight of the novel dalliance of one woman in a shared body, while concealment of one half prevents its complete enjoyment.
Having bowed to <s>Mataṅga</s>, <s>Bharata</s>, and the other foremost masters skilled in the science of beautiful song and music,

children.text: śrīkumbhakarṇanṛpatirvivṛtiṃ tanoti gānaṃ nidhāya sarasaṃ rasikapriyāhvām ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> sets forth an exposition of <s>Jayadeva</s>'s words, establishing melodious song and giving it the title <s>Rasikapriyā</s>.
There was a foremost twice-born man named <s>Bappa</s>, the finest member of the <s>Vaijayāyana</s> lineage.
By the favor of <s>Hara</s>, he became a king so that he might abundantly enjoy a realm free from decline.
In his lineage there shines that supreme rank which has vanquished the positions of disputants in logic,
in glorious <s>Medapāṭa</s>, foremost among the <s>Guhilas</s>, where kings were born.
There, in due succession within that lineage rich in noble descendants, arose a king named <s>Hammīra</s>,
as the wish-granting tree arose in the ocean together with its succession of heaps of jewels beginning with the moon.
Regarding every suppliant who approached him as a worthy recipient, he freely gave gifts multiplied without end.
Famed as a lion in difficult assaults, he made battles that struck fear into all his enemies.
From him was born a son rich in statecraft, devoted to the highest good, compassionate, and long-lived:
the illustrious <s>Kṣetrasiṃha</s>, a <s>Narasiṃha</s> against the men of the opposing side, a lion possessed of lofty pride.
After him arose <s>Lakṣa</s>, marked by exalted qualities and skilled in destroying yakṣa-like enemies,
a protector of the dharma established at <s>Gayā</s> for liberation, clear-sighted, who fulfilled every aim of the Three-eyed <s>Tryakṣa</s>.
His son, who obtained the earth through conduct surpassing that of former kings,
was the illustrious lord <s>Mokala</s>, whose lotus feet shone with the radiance of jewels upon the crowns of bowing enemies.
Thereafter King <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, equal to <s>Indra</s> in strength, supports the earth,

children.text: śeṣādikebhyo dharaṇe dharitryā bharasya viśrāṇitaviśramaḥ san ||
children.translated_text: granting <s>Śeṣa</s> and the other bearers repose from carrying the burden of the world.
Devoted to the worship of <s>Śrīśa</s>, accomplished in the science of music, and versed in all its branches,
he now sets forth a newly fashioned commentary on the beautiful songs of the illustrious <s>Gītagovinda</s>.
Having conquered the earth and made its rulers pay tribute,
this connoisseur now delights in the essence of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>.
The learned <s>Jayadeva</s> announced this work as a <s>prabandha</s> (structured musical composition),
but it has no defining character made evident through all of its constituent limbs.
Therefore, by joining it to the six limbs beginning with <s>svara</s> (musical pitch), one should bring it into a valid form.

children.text: nītvā gītvā tadā hitvā kuṭīkāsu pravartyate ||
children.translated_text: After it has been brought forth and sung, however, it is then abandoned and continues to circulate in small schools.

children.text: śṛṅgāre saprapañce rasa iha ruciraucityayuktau prakṛṣṭe 'laṃkāre nāyikāyā guṇagaṇagaṇane varṇane nāyakasya
children.translated_text: As for fully elaborated <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor) joined with pleasing propriety, excellent <s>alaṃkāra</s> (poetic ornament), the enumeration of a heroine's many qualities, and the description of a hero—

children.text: gītau prītau ca vṛttau layamanu rasikāḥ kautukaṃ cet tademā doṣairmuktā guṇāḍhyāḥ śṛṇuta narapateḥ kumbhakarṇasya vācaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and as for song, love, meter, and rhythm—if connoisseurs are curious about these, then listen to these faultless, richly accomplished words of King <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.

children.text: sa kiṃ bandhaḥ ślāghyo vrajati śithilībhāvamasakṛdvicāreṇākṣipto nanu bhavati ṭīkāpi kimu sā
children.translated_text: What composition deserves praise if, repeatedly challenged by critical examination, it becomes loose and incoherent? And what indeed is that commentary...
